answer_text:
Let \(N=R/(x^2)=\mathbb{Q}[x]/(x^2)\). An \(R\)-linear map
\[
\phi: M=\operatorname{coker}(R^2\xrightarrow{A}R^2)\to N
\]
is the same as an \(R\)-linear map \(\psi:R^2\to N\) that vanishes on the image of \(A\).

Write
\[
\psi(e_1)=a,\qquad \psi(e_2)=b
\]
with \(a,b\in N\). The columns of \(A\) are
\[
\begin{pmatrix}x-1\\1-x\end{pmatrix},\qquad \begin{pmatrix}0\\x^2\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Thus we need
\[
\psi\!\left(\begin{pmatrix}x-1\\1-x\end{pmatrix}\right)
=(x-1)a+(1-x)b
=(x-1)(a-b)=0
\]
and
\[
\psi\!\left(\begin{pmatrix}0\\x^2\end{pmatrix}\right)=x^2b=0.
\]
In \(N=R/(x^2)\), the second condition is automatic because \(x^2=0\). Also \(x-1\) is a unit in \(N\), since
\[
(x-1)(-1-x)=1-x^2\equiv 1 \pmod{x^2}.
\]
Therefore \((x-1)(a-b)=0\) implies \(a=b\).

So
\[
\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,N)\cong N=\mathbb{Q}[x]/(x^2).
\]
As a \(\mathbb{Q}\)-vector space, \(\mathbb{Q}[x]/(x^2)\) has basis \(\{1,x\}\), hence dimension \(2\).

Thus the rank is
\[
\boxed{2}.
\]
